and a new paragraph (bi  \nis added as set out below."},{"char_end":24300,"char_start":23863,"text":"Doc. 59-3976; Filed, May 11, 1959;\n8:47 a.m.]\nPART 26 —  EMPLOYMENT WITH  \nPUBLIC INTERNATIONAL ORGAN­\nIZATIONS\nPart 26 is revised and amended to read  \nas follows:\nSubpart A— Detail and Transfer of Federal Em­\nployees to Public International Organizations  \nG eneral  P rovisions\nSec.\n26.101 Purpose.\n26.102 Definitions.\n26.103 Effective date of regulations.\n26.104 Election' procedures.\n26.105 Organizations to which regulations\napply."},{"char_end":26063,"char_start":25483,"text":"For the purpose of this subpart, the  \nterm:\n(a) “Act” means the Federal Employ­\nees International Organization Service  \nAct. -\n(b) “Agency” means any “Federal  \nagency,” as defined in section 2 of the  \nAct. ,\n(c) “Commission” means the United  \nStates Civil Service Commission.\n«  (d) “Term of employment” means not  \nmore than (1) three consecutive years of  \nemployment, or (2) the period of less  \nthan three years specified at the time of  \nconsent to transfer, beginning with en­\ntrance on duty in the international  \norganization.\n§ 26.103 Effective date o f regulations."},{"char_end":26239,"char_start":26064,"text":"The regulations in this part are effec­\ntive August 28, 1958, and as of that date  \nrevoke and supersede the. regulations of  \nthis part in effect immediately prior  \nthereto."},{"char_end":30251,"char_start":30232,"text":"(c) Effective date."},{"char_end":30402,"char_start":30253,"text":"The effective date\nof the transfer shall be established by  \nmutual agreement between the agency  \nand the organization. *\n(d) Recording requirement."},{"char_end":36756,"char_start":36594,"text":"Decisions favorable to the appel­\nlant may be made retroactively effective  \nto the expiration of the agency’ s thirty  \nday time limit for effecting restoration."},{"char_end":65482,"char_start":64764,"text":"It is hereby found that good cause  \nexists for not postponing the effective  \ndate of this revision beyond that there­\nin specified (5 U.S.C. 1003(c)) in that:\n(1) The 1959 processing season for  \nfrozen peas is imminent and it is neces­\nsary for purposes of inspection and mar­\nketing that these revised standards be  \nmade effective at the beginning of the  \nprocessing season; (2) changes made  \nwere based upon data and comments  \nfrom the industry and found to be in  \nthe best interest of the industry as well  \nas the consumer; and (3) the industry  \nhas been apprised of the changes and  \ncompliance therewith will not require any  \nspecial preparation that cannot be com­\npleted by the effective time hereof."},{"char_end":65827,"char_start":65483,"text":"The United States Standards for  \nGrades of Frozen Peas (which is the  \nsixth issue) contained in this subpart  \nshall become effective fifteen days after  \nthe date of publication in the F ederal \nR egister and thereupon will supersede  \nthe United States Standards for Grades  \nof Frozen Peas which have been in effect  \nsince March 15, 1945."},{"char_end":66686,"char_start":65919,"text":"Doc. 59-3990; Filed, May 11, 1959;\n8:48 a.m.]\nChapter IX— Agricultural Marketing  \nService (Marketing Agreements and  \nOrders), Department of Agriculture\nPART 953— LEMONS GROWN IN  \nCALIFORNIA AND ARIZONA\nSubpart— Rules and Regulations \nR evision\nNotice was published in the F ederal \nR egister issue of April 22, 1959 (24 F.R.  \n3115), that the Department was giving  \nconsideration to a proposed revision of  \nthe rules and regulations (Subpart—  \nLemon Administrative Committee Rules  \nand Regulations; 7 CFR 953.100 et seq.),  \ncurrently in effect pursuant to the ap­\nplicable provisions of the marketing  \nagreement, as amended, and Order No.  \n53, as amended (7 CFR Part 953; 23 F.R.  \n9053), regulating the handling of lemons  \ngrown in California and Arizona."},{"char_end":66816,"char_start":66687,"text":"This  \nregulatory program is effective under the  \nAgricultural Marketing Agreement Act  \nof 1937, as amended (7 U.S.C. 601-674)."},{"char_end":85587,"char_start":85393,"text":"Allotment loans shall be deemed  \nrepaid if such loans fall due in a week  \nduring which there is no limitation on  \nlemon shipments in effect pursuant to  \n§^53.52, for the particular district."},{"char_end":90054,"char_start":89911,"text":"As required by  \n§  953.67, all handling of such lemons  \nshall be subject to, and limited by, allot­\nment when volume regulation is in effect."},{"char_end":102298,"char_start":101595,"text":"Pursuant to the market­\ning agreement, as amended, and Order  \nNo. 53, as amended (7 CFR Part 953),\nregulating the handling of lemons grown  \nin California and Arizona, effective under  \nthe applicable provisions of the Agricul­\ntural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937,  \nas amended (7 U.S.Ç. 601 et seq.; 68  \nStat. 906, 1047), and upon the basis of  \nthe recommendation and information  \nsubmitted by the Lemon Administrative  \nCommittee, established under the said  \namended marketing agreement and or­\nder, and upon other available informa­\ntion, it is hereby found that the  \nlimitation of handling of such lemons as  \nhereinafter provided will tend to effec­\ntuate the declared policy of the act.\n2."},{"char_end":103037,"char_start":102299,"text":"It is hereby further found that it  \nis impracticable and contrary to the  \npublic interest to give preliminary notice,  \nengage in public rule-making procedure,  \nand postpone the effective date of this  \namendment until 30 days after publica­\ntion hereof in the F ederal R egister (60 \nStat. 237; 5 U.S.C. 1001 et seq.) because  \nthe time intervening between the date  \nwhen information upon which this  \namendment is based became available  \nand the time when this amendment must  \nbecome effective in order to effectuate  \nthe deolared policy, of the Agricultural  \nMarketing Agreement Act of 1937, as  \namended, is insufficient, and this amend­\nment relieves restriction on the handling  \nof lemons grown in California and  \nArizona."},{"char_end":115091,"char_start":114958,"text":"(Sec. 103, 66 Stat. 173; 8 U.S.C. 1103)\nThis order shall become effective on  \nthe date of its publication in the F ederal \nRegister."},{"char_end":115396,"char_start":115092,"text":"Compliance with the provi­\nsions of section 4 of the Administrative  \nProcedure Act (60 Stat. 238; 5 U.S.C.  \n1003) as to notice of proposed rule mak­\ning and delayed effective date is unnec­\nessary in this instance because the rules  \nprescribed by the order relate to agency  \nprocedure and management."},{"char_end":116588,"char_start":116314,"text":"Because this amendment deals with  \nprocedural rules and immediate effec­\ntiveness thereof will not adversely affect  \nany person, the Commission has found  \nthat good cause exists why this amend­\nment should be made effective without  \nthe customary period of prior notice."},{"char_end":116814,"char_start":116591,"text":"Pursuant to the Administrative Proce­\ndure Act, Public Law 404, 79th Congress,  \n2d Sess., Title 10, Code of Federal Regu­\nlations, Part' 2 is amended as follows,  \neffective upon publication in the F ederal \nR egister :\n1."},{"char_end":120256,"char_start":119740,"text":"Accordingly, as authorized and re­\nquired by section 8 of the Fair Labor  \nStandards Act of 1938, as amended (52  \nStat. 1064, as amended; 29 U.S.C. 208),  \nReorganization Plan No. 6 of 1950 (64  \nStat. 1263; 3 CFR, 1950 Supp., p. 165),  \nand General Order No. 45-A of the Sec­\nretary of Labor (15 F.R. 3290), the rec­\nommendations of the committee are  \nhereby published in this order amending  \n29 CFR, Part 601, effective May 28, 1959,  \nto read as follows:\nSec.\n602.1 Definition.\n602.2 Wage rates.\n602.3 Notices."},{"char_end":130189,"char_start":129975,"text":"Taylor, shall, be the bases for determin­\ning effective horsepower required, M a n d a to r y  R e v ie w  o f E x e m p te d  M a te r ia l All classified infor­\nmation and material originated after the effective date of this order \nwhich is exempted under (B) above from the General Declassification \nSchedule shall be subject to a classification review by the originating \nDepartment at any time after the expiration of ten years from the date \nof origin provided:\n( 1  ) A Department or member of the public requests a review;\n(2) The request describes the record with sufficient particularity to \nenable the Department to identify it;*and\n(3) The record can be obtained with only a reasonable amount of \neffort."},{"char_end":17264,"char_start":17021,"text":"Information or material classified before the \neffective date of this order and which is assigned to Group 4 under \nExecutive Order No. 10501, as amended by Executive Order No. 10964, \nshall be subject to the General Declassification Schedule."},{"char_end":17505,"char_start":17265,"text":"All other infor­\nmation or material classified before the effective date of this order, \nwhether or not assigned to Groups 1, 2, or 3 of Executive Order \nNo. 10501, as amended, shall be excluded from the General Declassifica­\ntion Schedule."},{"char_end":17833,"char_start":17506,"text":"However, at any time after the expiration of ten years \nfrom the date of origin it shall be subject to a mandatory classification \nreview and disposition uncfer the same conditions and criteria that apply \nto classified information and material created after the effective date of \nthis order as set forth in (B) and (G) above."},{"char_end":18733,"char_start":17943,"text":"All classified information or material which is thirty years \nold or more, whether originating before or after the effective date of \nthis order, shall be declassified under the following conditions:\n( 1  ) All information and material classified after the effective date of \nthis order shall, whether or not declassification has been requested, \nbecome automatically declassified at the end of thirty full calendar years \nafter the date of its original classification except for such specifically \nidentified information or material which the head of the originating \nDepartment personally determines in writing at that time to require \ncontinued protection because such continued protection is essential to \nthe national security or disclosure would place a person in immediate \njeopardy."},{"char_end":19184,"char_start":18835,"text":"(2) All information and material classified before the effective date \nof this order and more than thirty years old shall be systematically \nreviewed for declassification by the Archivist of the United States by the \nend of the thirtieth full calendar year following the year in which it was\nFEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 37, NO. 48— FRIDAY, MARCH 10, 1972"},{"char_end":23963,"char_start":23626,"text":"(B) To promote the baric purposes of this order, the head of each \nDepartment originating or handling classified information or material \nshall:\n( 1  ) Prior to the effective date of this order submit to the Interagency \nClassification Review Committee for approval a copy of the regulations \nit proposes to adopt pursuant to this order."},{"char_end":30433,"char_start":30093,"text":"Executive Order \nNo. 10501 of November 5, 1953, as amended by Executive Orders No. \n10816 of May 8, 1959, No. 10901 of January 11, 1961, No. 10964 of \nSeptember 20, 1961, No. 10985 of January 15, 1962, No. 11097 of \nMarch 6,1963 and by Section 1  (a) of No. 11382 of November 28, 1967, \nis superseded as of the effective date of this order."},{"char_end":30520,"char_start":30469,"text":"This order shall become effective on June 1,
